# Compile Epic Context

**Task**
Given an epic number, the epics file, the planning artifacts directory, and a desired output path, compile a clean, focused, developer-ready context file (`epic-<N>-context.md`).

**Steps**

1. Read the epics file and extract the target epic's title, goal, and list of stories.
2. Scan the planning artifacts directory for the standard files (PRD, architecture, UX/design, product brief).
3. Pull only the information relevant to this epic.
4. Write the compiled context to the exact output path using the format below.

## Exact Output Format

Use these headings:

```markdown
# Epic {N} Context: {Epic Title}

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

{One clear paragraph: what this epic achieves and why it matters.}

## Stories

- Story X.Y: Brief title only
- ...

## Requirements & Constraints

{Relevant functional/non-functional requirements and success criteria for this epic (describe by purpose, not source).}

## Technical Decisions

{Key architecture decisions, constraints, patterns, data models, and conventions relevant to this epic.}

## UX & Interaction Patterns

{Relevant UX flows, interaction patterns, and design constraints (omit section entirely if nothing relevant).}

## Cross-Story Dependencies

{Dependencies between stories in this epic or with other epics/systems (omit if none).}
```

## Rules

- **Scope aggressively.** Include only what a developer working on any story in this epic actually needs. When in doubt, leave it out — the developer can always read the full planning doc.
- **Describe by purpose, not by source.** Write "API responses must include pagination metadata" not "Per PRD section 3.2.1, pagination is required." Planning doc internals will change; the constraint won't.
- **No full copies.** Never quote source documents, section numbers, or paste large blocks verbatim. Always distill.
- **No story-level details.** The story list is for orientation only. Individual story specs handle the details.
- **Nothing derivable from the codebase.** Don't document what a developer can learn by reading the code.
- **Be concise and actionable.** Target 800–1500 tokens total. This file loads into build's context alongside other material.
- **Never hallucinate content.** If source material doesn't say something, don't invent it.
- **Omit empty sections entirely**, except Goal and Stories, which are always required.

## Error handling

- **If the epics file is missing or the target epic is not found:** write nothing and report the problem to the calling agent. Goal and Stories cannot be populated without a usable epics file.
- **If planning artifacts are missing or empty:** still produce the file with Goal and Stories populated from the epics file, and note the gap in the Goal section. Never hallucinate content to fill missing sections.

1	# Epic 4 Context: Timeline & History
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Users can see every Entry they've ever captured, from any source (text, audio, photo), in one chronological view grouped by date, each carrying a live per-entry sync status — and never lose track of something they wrote, even offline or mid-session-expiry. This is the first independently demoable milestone built on top of the `entries` feature Epic 3 introduced: a working, origin-marked timeline with reconciling sync badges, with no search or filtering yet (that's Epic 5). Depends on Epic 3 (there is nothing to list until Entries exist).
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking
12	- Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge
13	- Story 4.3: Empty-State Handling
14	- Story 4.4: Entry Detail View
15	
16	## Requirements & Constraints
17	
18	- All Entries from every source are listed together in one list, grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
19	- A list load that exceeds the loading-indicator threshold (300ms) shows a skeleton loading state; under that threshold, no loading UI appears at all.
20	- Zero Entries renders a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture — never a blank list.
21	- A single Entry can be opened to view its full content; there is no edit affordance anywhere on that screen, and no update/delete capability exists for Entries at all — read-only, permanently.
22	- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns a generic not-found outcome, never a distinguishable permission-denied code; the UI must treat both identically.
23	- The sync badge has exactly three states (Synchronizing / Synchronization error / Synchronized), derived client-side only — the backend has no sync-status field. A freshly created Entry starts Synchronizing until the write is confirmed, then flips to Synchronized. A failed write (network or any error code) shows Synchronization error until a later successful write reconciles it.
24	- Tapping an error badge retries that Entry's write when the underlying error is retryable; when it isn't, it shows an inline explanation instead — never a dead retry button.
25	- The sync-badge update stream is fully independent of the auth/session stream: a pending sync transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling, and the session-expiry overlay must be able to appear over this screen without crashing or losing scroll position.
26	- This feature's screen composes three data streams (auth status, sync-badge state, Entry data) only through the domain layer — no BLoC/Cubit here ever references another BLoC/Cubit directly.
27	- No swipe gesture is implemented on a record card (Entries are immutable, so no gesture may imply an edit/delete that doesn't exist).
28	- Color is never the sole carrier of sync-badge state — always paired with an accessible label, and the retry hit area must be ≥44pt even though the dot itself is small.
29	
30	## Technical Decisions
31	
32	- `entries/domain` (introduced in Epic 3) already owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port, and the Hive box; this epic extends that same port with read/list operations rather than introducing a second Entry model or owner.
33	- `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only, permanently — no update/delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of a mutating entries endpoint.
34	- One single derivation function lives in `entries/domain` computing the sync badge from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state (no pending write → Synchronized; write in flight → Synchronizing; failed write → Synchronization error). Every screen that ever renders this badge (this timeline now, chat's save confirmation later) consumes that one function's output — none recomputes it inline.
35	- This screen's composite state (auth × sync × data) is its own sealed state class, not the shared generic single-fetch `Resource<T>` type used elsewhere — it has a composite, multi-stream lifecycle `Resource<T>` isn't meant for.
36	- Reads fall back transparently to the local Hive cache when offline; the cache stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — never locally filtered, joined, sorted, or re-derived. Pagination uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim, cached alongside the box it pages.
37	- A badge retry re-attempts the same underlying write call that originally failed; there is no separate retry endpoint for entries.
38

# Epic 4 Context: Timeline & History

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users can see every Entry they've ever captured, from any source (text, audio, photo), in one chronological view grouped by date, each carrying a live per-entry sync status — and never lose track of something they wrote, even offline or mid-session-expiry. This is the first independently demoable milestone built on top of the `entries` feature Epic 3 introduced: a working, origin-marked timeline with reconciling sync badges, with no search or filtering yet (that's Epic 5). Depends on Epic 3 (there is nothing to list until Entries exist).

## Stories

- Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking
- Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge
- Story 4.3: Empty-State Handling
- Story 4.4: Entry Detail View

## Requirements & Constraints

- All Entries from every source are listed together in one list, grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
- A list load that exceeds the loading-indicator threshold (300ms) shows a skeleton loading state; under that threshold, no loading UI appears at all.
- Zero Entries renders a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture — never a blank list.
- A single Entry can be opened to view its full content; there is no edit affordance anywhere on that screen, and no update/delete capability exists for Entries at all — read-only, permanently.
- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns a generic not-found outcome, never a distinguishable permission-denied code; the UI must treat both identically.
- The sync badge has exactly three states (Synchronizing / Synchronization error / Synchronized), derived client-side only — the backend has no sync-status field. A freshly created Entry starts Synchronizing until the write is confirmed, then flips to Synchronized. A failed write (network or any error code) shows Synchronization error until a later successful write reconciles it.
- Tapping an error badge retries that Entry's write when the underlying error is retryable; when it isn't, it shows an inline explanation instead — never a dead retry button.
- The sync-badge update stream is fully independent of the auth/session stream: a pending sync transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling, and the session-expiry overlay must be able to appear over this screen without crashing or losing scroll position.
- This feature's screen composes three data streams (auth status, sync-badge state, Entry data) only through the domain layer — no BLoC/Cubit here ever references another BLoC/Cubit directly.
- No swipe gesture is implemented on a record card (Entries are immutable, so no gesture may imply an edit/delete that doesn't exist).
- Color is never the sole carrier of sync-badge state — always paired with an accessible label, and the retry hit area must be ≥44pt even though the dot itself is small.

## Technical Decisions

- `entries/domain` (introduced in Epic 3) already owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port, and the Hive box; this epic extends that same port with read/list operations rather than introducing a second Entry model or owner.
- `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only, permanently — no update/delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of a mutating entries endpoint.
- One single derivation function lives in `entries/domain` computing the sync badge from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state (no pending write → Synchronized; write in flight → Synchronizing; failed write → Synchronization error). Every screen that ever renders this badge (this timeline now, chat's save confirmation later) consumes that one function's output — none recomputes it inline.
- This screen's composite state (auth × sync × data) is its own sealed state class, not the shared generic single-fetch `Resource<T>` type used elsewhere — it has a composite, multi-stream lifecycle `Resource<T>` isn't meant for.
- Reads fall back transparently to the local Hive cache when offline; the cache stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — never locally filtered, joined, sorted, or re-derived. Pagination uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim, cached alongside the box it pages.
- A badge retry re-attempts the same underlying write call that originally failed; there is no separate retry endpoint for entries.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Record card spine color encodes origin: manual = primary color, audio = olive green, photo = gray (chat's accent color is reserved for Epic 6's chat-saved entries).
- The prototype shows the record card as otherwise display-only — tapping it previously did nothing beyond surfacing the badge's retry affordance in the error state. The detail view this epic adds (FR-18) has no prototype precedent; build it minimal and strictly read-only, consistent with the record card's established "no edit/expand implied" convention.
- Skeleton rows use the shared skeleton-loading component (never a spinner) and only appear past the 300ms threshold.
- Empty state must offer a concrete CTA back into the capture flow (opens the Insertion Modal), not just explanatory copy.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Depends on Epic 3: the `entries` feature, `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository.create`, and the entries Hive box must already exist; this epic only adds read/list.
- Reuses Epic 1's session-expiry overlay (FR-2) as-is for mid-timeline session expiry — no new overlay is built here.
- The sync-badge derivation function built in Story 4.2 is a shared dependency: Epic 6 (chat's save-to-journal confirmation) consumes the same function rather than building its own.
- Epic 5 (Semantic Search & Filtering) is built directly on top of this epic's timeline surface and extends the same `EntriesRepository` port further with search — do not duplicate list/display logic there.

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.

13:The prototype has **32 navigable states**, reachable from a single state machine (a `screen` variable plus overlay flags). Not every state is a new full screen — several are **overlays** (modal, sheet, bottom sheet, dialog) shown on top of one of three base screens: **Home/Chat**, **Meus Registros** and **Configurações**. Overlays preserve the screen underneath (it stays visible, with a darkened scrim behind).
25:  ├─ overlay: side menu (☰ icon) ──> Meus Registros | Planos de Ação | Configurações | new conversation
26:  └─ overlay: Insertion modal ("+" button) ──> tabs Texto / Áudio / Foto, each with its own sub-states
29:Meus Registros (base screen, from the side menu)
30:  ├─ empty state (no records) ──CTA "Criar primeiro registro"──> Insertion modal
48:Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.
65:| Tela 1 — Insight | Insight card with ochre spine, label "INSIGHT", "x" to dismiss, interleaved in the messages. |
70:| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |
73:Common structure: "x" to close and a 3-tab bar (Texto / Áudio / Foto); the active tab has a filled dark-green background.
80:| Áudio — Transcrito | Editable transcribed text; original audio duration in mono; "Salvar" enabled. |
82:| Foto — Captura | Two large buttons, "Câmera" and "Galeria". |
83:| Foto — Processando OCR | Photo thumbnail, spinner, "Reconhecendo texto...". |
84:| Foto — Reconhecido | Small thumbnail next to the extracted (editable) text; "Salvar". |
85:| Foto — Erro | Thumbnail kept, warning icon, "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto", button "Tentar novamente" and secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". |

`elevation1` — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)` (cards at rest) · `elevation2` — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)` (sheets, modals).

Phosphor library, Regular style, 24 dp: `list`, `plus`, `magnifying-glass`, `funnel`, `bookmark-simple`, `microphone`, `camera`, `gear`, `kanban`, `notebook`, `fingerprint`, `lightbulb` (and others used on specific screens: `check`, `warning-circle`, `wifi-slash`, `circle-notch`, `caret-left`, `download-simple`, `pencil-simple`, `x`, `stop`, `image`, `check-circle`, `chart-line-up`, `backspace`, `lock-key`, `paper-plane-tilt`, `chat-circle-text`).

### Spine (colored bar on the left of a card) — 3 contexts
1. Proactive insight in the chat — ochre.
2. Entry origin in "Meus Registros" — color by type: manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre.
3. Kanban column in "Planos de Ação" — color by column **[ext]**.

### Micro-animations and transitions
- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
- Continuous spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state.
- Text streaming: the AI response is revealed progressively, with a blinking cursor at the end while it is "typing".
- PIN: after the 4th digit, a 350 ms pause before navigating.

---

## 4. Special states that need extra care

- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.

---

## 5. Implementation notes

1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

---
title: 'Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Entries created via text/audio/photo capture (Epic 3) have nowhere to be seen — "Meus Registros" is still the Epic 1 throwaway placeholder, and `EntriesRepository` only supports `create`.

**Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a real screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by calendar day, each card visually marked by capture origin. **Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by day, each card marked by origin. Extend `EntriesRepository` with paginated `list()`, falling back to Hive when offline. No sync badge, no tap-to-detail, no search/filter — those are 4.2/4.4/Epic 5.

- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.

---
title: 'Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'ready-for-dev'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Entries from text/audio/photo capture (Epic 3) are invisible — "Meus Registros" is still the Epic 1 placeholder, and `EntriesRepository` only has `create`.

**Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by day, each card marked by origin. Extend `EntriesRepository` with paginated `list()`, falling back to Hive when offline. No sync badge, no tap-to-detail, no search/filter — those are 4.2/4.4/Epic 5.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.list({cursor, limit = 20})` → `Either<Failure, EntriesPage>`. Server assumed newest-first by `occurredAt` (undocumented, decided per AGENTS.md policy).
- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` → fall back to a full `entries` Hive box dump, sorted `occurredAt` desc, `nextCursor: null`. Other failures propagate as `Left`.
- Successful page persists to the Hive box, same "persist then return" shape `create()` uses.
- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.
- Card spine by `EntrySource`, exact hex match to prototype's `sourceMeta`: manual→`colorPrimary`, audio→`colorSecondary`, photo→`colorTextSecondary`, chat→`colorAccent`. Plus source icon, time, excerpt. No badge, not tappable.
- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.

**Ask First:** None — open calls are pinned above.

**Never:** sync badge (4.2), tap/detail nav (4.4), filters/search (Epic 5, tags), pull-to-refresh, any repository method beyond `list`/`create`, polished empty-state CTA (4.3 — plain "no entries" text only).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| First load, online | Screen opens | Skeleton past 300ms, then grouped list | N/A |
| Scroll pagination | Near list end, `nextCursor != null` | Next page appended, no dup ids | Fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry |
| Offline fallback | `list()` returns offline/timeout | Cached entries shown, sorted desc | N/A |
| Other failure | e.g. `authExpired` | Error state rendered | Global overlay or inline retry |
| Zero entries | Empty page + empty cache | Plain "no entries yet" text | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list()` to the one-method port
- `entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` -- `occurredAt` stays raw ISO string, parsed only for grouping
- `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` -- `create()`'s mirror shape for `list()`
- `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- `create()`'s call/error-map shape to mirror
- `entries/entries_injection.dart` -- add `MeusRegistrosCubit` registration
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` -- `get(function, {queryParameters})` already fits
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` -- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` = fallback triggers
- `lib/core/resource.dart` -- doc excludes RF07 from `Resource<T>`
- `app_router.dart:118-120`, `placeholder_screens.dart:159-182` -- route + placeholder
- `placeholder_screens.dart:355-397` (`_KanbanCard`) -- spine-card structure to mirror
- `placeholder_screens.dart:18-58` (`BootSplashScreen`) -- 300ms skeleton-delay pattern
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` -- reused as-is
- `openapi.yaml:480-645` -- `entries-list`: `cursor`/`limit`, `{data, meta.nextCursor}`

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `entries/domain/entities/entries_page.dart` -- new `EntriesPage{items, nextCursor}`
- [ ] `entries/domain/entities/entry_date_group.dart` -- new `EntryDateGroup{date, entries}` + pure `groupEntriesByDate()`
- [ ] `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list({cursor, limit = 20})`
- [ ] `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `list()` via `ApiClient.get('entries-list', ...)`
- [ ] `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` -- implement `list()` incl. offline fallback
- [ ] `lib/core/widgets/skeleton_box.dart` -- new generic shimmer, tokens-only
- [ ] `entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- new, `loadFirstPage()`/`loadMore()`
- [ ] `entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart` -- new, mirrors `_KanbanCard`, no tap handler
- [ ] `entries/presentation/widgets/entry_skeleton_card.dart` -- new, from `SkeletonBox`
- [ ] `entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart` -- new, scroll pagination + skeleton delay + grouped list
- [ ] `entries/entries_injection.dart` -- register `MeusRegistrosCubit` as `lazySingleton`
- [ ] `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` -- route builds `MeusRegistrosScreen(cubit: sl())`
- [ ] `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` -- delete `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen`
- [ ] Tests: grouping edge cases (midnight boundary, empty), `list()` datasource/repository incl. offline, cubit, screen (skeleton timing, pagination, zero/error)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a successful load with multi-day entries, when rendered, then the list is grouped by day with each card's spine colored by `EntrySource`.
- Given offline, when the screen loads, then cached entries render with no crash or duplicates.
- Given a session expiry while visible, when the global overlay appears, then scroll position is preserved and nothing throws.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- Airplane mode with entries cached, reopen screen, confirm cached list renders instead of an error.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.list({cursor, limit = 20})` → `Either<Failure, EntriesPage>`. Server assumed newest-first by `occurredAt` (undocumented, decided per AGENTS.md policy).
- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` → fall back to a full `entries` Hive box dump, sorted `occurredAt` desc, `nextCursor: null`. Other failures propagate as `Left`.
- Successful page persists to the Hive box, same "persist then return" shape `create()` uses.
- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.
- Card spine by `EntrySource`, exact hex match to prototype's `sourceMeta`: manual→`colorPrimary`, audio→`colorSecondary`, photo→`colorTextSecondary`, chat→`colorAccent`. Plus source icon, time, excerpt. No badge, not tappable.
- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.

**Ask First:** None — open calls are pinned above.

**Never:** sync badge (4.2), tap/detail nav (4.4), filters/search (Epic 5, tags), pull-to-refresh, any repository method beyond `list`/`create`, polished empty-state CTA (4.3 — plain "no entries" text only).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| First load, online | Screen opens | Skeleton past 300ms, then grouped list | N/A |
| Scroll pagination | Near list end, `nextCursor != null` | Next page appended, no dup ids | Fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry |
| Offline fallback | `list()` returns offline/timeout | Cached entries shown, sorted desc | N/A |
| Other failure | e.g. `authExpired` | Error state rendered | Global overlay or inline retry |
| Zero entries | Empty page + empty cache | Plain "no entries yet" text | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list()` to the one-method port
- `entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` -- `occurredAt` stays raw ISO string, parsed only for grouping
- `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` -- `create()`'s mirror shape for `list()`
- `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- `create()`'s call/error-map shape to mirror
- `entries/entries_injection.dart` -- add `MeusRegistrosCubit` registration
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` -- `get(function, {queryParameters})` already fits
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` -- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` = fallback triggers
- `lib/core/resource.dart` -- doc excludes RF07 from `Resource<T>`
- `app_router.dart:118-120`, `placeholder_screens.dart:159-182` -- route + placeholder
- `placeholder_screens.dart:355-397` (`_KanbanCard`) -- spine-card structure to mirror
- `placeholder_screens.dart:18-58` (`BootSplashScreen`) -- 300ms skeleton-delay pattern
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` -- reused as-is
- `openapi.yaml:480-645` -- `entries-list`: `cursor`/`limit`, `{data, meta.nextCursor}`

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `entries/domain/entities/entries_page.dart` -- new `EntriesPage{items, nextCursor}`
- [ ] `entries/domain/entities/entry_date_group.dart` -- new `EntryDateGroup{date, entries}` + pure `groupEntriesByDate()`
- [ ] `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list({cursor, limit = 20})`
- [ ] `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `list()` via `ApiClient.get('entries-list', ...)`
- [ ] `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` -- implement `list()` incl. offline fallback
- [ ] `lib/core/widgets/skeleton_box.dart` -- new generic shimmer, tokens-only
- [ ] `entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- new, `loadFirstPage()`/`loadMore()`
- [ ] `entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart` -- new, mirrors `_KanbanCard`, no tap handler
- [ ] `entries/presentation/widgets/entry_skeleton_card.dart` -- new, from `SkeletonBox`
- [ ] `entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart` -- new, scroll pagination + skeleton delay + grouped list
- [ ] `entries/entries_injection.dart` -- register `MeusRegistrosCubit` as `lazySingleton`
- [ ] `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` -- route builds `MeusRegistrosScreen(cubit: sl())`
- [ ] `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` -- delete `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen`
- [ ] Tests: grouping edge cases (midnight boundary, empty), `list()` datasource/repository incl. offline, cubit, screen (skeleton timing, pagination, zero/error)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a successful load with multi-day entries, when rendered, then the list is grouped by day with each card's spine colored by `EntrySource`.
- Given offline, when the screen loads, then cached entries render with no crash or duplicates.
- Given a session expiry while visible, when the global overlay appears, then scroll position is preserved and nothing throws.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- Airplane mode with entries cached, reopen screen, confirm cached list renders instead of an error.

- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.

# Verification Gap Review

**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.

The main verification gap shapes are:

1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.

## Evidence Rules

- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.

## Review Sequence

### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change

Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.

Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.

Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.

If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).

### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed

Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.

Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.

### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used

Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.

Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.

### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test

For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.

A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.

Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.

- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.

A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.

For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.

Common patterns:

- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.

### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real

Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.

Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.

Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.

Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.

## OUTPUT FORMAT

Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.

```markdown
### <one-line title naming the gap>

- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
- **Existing test evidence:**
  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
- **Demonstration:**
  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
```

If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:

```markdown
## Other findings

- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
```

When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:

`No verification gaps found.`

## CONTENT SOURCE

Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you. If none is supplied, stop with exactly: `No verification gaps found.`

## Intent

**Problem:** Entries from text/audio/photo capture (Epic 3) are invisible — "Meus Registros" is still the Epic 1 placeholder, and `EntriesRepository` only has `create`.

**Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by day, each card marked by origin. Extend `EntriesRepository` with paginated `list()`, falling back to Hive when offline. No sync badge, no tap-to-detail, no search/filter — those are 4.2/4.4/Epic 5.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.list({cursor, limit = 20})` → `Either<Failure, EntriesPage>`. Server assumed newest-first by `occurredAt` (undocumented, decided per AGENTS.md policy).
- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` → fall back to a full `entries` Hive box dump, sorted `occurredAt` desc, `nextCursor: null`. Other failures propagate as `Left`.
- Successful page persists to the Hive box, same "persist then return" shape `create()` uses.
- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.
- Card spine by `EntrySource`, exact hex match to prototype's `sourceMeta`: manual→`colorPrimary`, audio→`colorSecondary`, photo→`colorTextSecondary`, chat→`colorAccent`. Plus source icon, time, excerpt. No badge, not tappable.
- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.

**Ask First:** None — open calls are pinned above.

**Never:** sync badge (4.2), tap/detail nav (4.4), filters/search (Epic 5, tags), pull-to-refresh, any repository method beyond `list`/`create`, polished empty-state CTA (4.3 — plain "no entries" text only).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| First load, online | Screen opens | Skeleton past 300ms, then grouped list | N/A |
| Scroll pagination | Near list end, `nextCursor != null` | Next page appended, no dup ids | Fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry |
| Offline fallback | `list()` returns offline/timeout | Cached entries shown, sorted desc | N/A |
| Other failure | e.g. `authExpired` | Error state rendered | Global overlay or inline retry |
| Zero entries | Empty page + empty cache | Plain "no entries yet" text | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

- `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list()` to the one-method port
- `entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` -- `occurredAt` stays raw ISO string, parsed only for grouping

- `placeholder_screens.dart:355-397` (`_KanbanCard`) -- spine-card structure to mirror
- `placeholder_screens.dart:18-58` (`BootSplashScreen`) -- 300ms skeleton-delay pattern
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` -- reused as-is
- `openapi.yaml:480-645` -- `entries-list`: `cursor`/`limit`, `{data, meta.nextCursor}`

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `entries/domain/entities/entries_page.dart` -- new `EntriesPage{items, nextCursor}`
- [x] `entries/domain/entities/entry_date_group.dart` -- new `EntryDateGroup{date, entries}` + pure `groupEntriesByDate()`

__RESUME_AGENT__:a2801b395c92089fb

Code review of your spec-4-1 implementation (chronological entry list with origin marking) surfaced the following confirmed patch findings. Apply all of them, then re-run the spec's Verification commands (`fvm flutter analyze`, `fvm flutter test`) and fix anything that breaks.

1. **Offline/timeout fallback during pagination corrupts pagination state** — `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart`'s `list()`. Currently `_offlineFallback()` fires for `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` regardless of `cursor`. Scope it to `cursor == null` only (the first/fresh-page request). When `cursor != null` (a `loadMore()` continuation) and the remote call fails with `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout`, propagate it as `Left` like any other failure — so `MeusRegistrosCubit._fetchMore()`'s existing `loadMoreFailed`/retry path handles it, matching the spec's "Scroll pagination: fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry" row instead of silently merging an unrelated full-cache dump into the paginated list (which also breaks the newest-first ordering `groupEntriesByDate()` relies on). The spec's Design Notes section now documents this clarification. Add a test exercising `list(cursor: 'x')` while offline/timeout confirming it now returns `Left`, alongside the existing no-cursor fallback tests.

2. **Stale async result can overwrite fresher state (no generation guard)** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart`. Neither `loadFirstPage()` nor `_fetchMore()` guards against an older in-flight call's result landing after a newer call already changed the state (e.g. user leaves and re-enters `/meus-registros` quickly while a slow request is still in flight, or taps retry while the original request hasn't resolved yet). Add a simple monotonic generation counter (e.g. `int _generation = 0`), incremented at the start of `loadFirstPage()`; capture it locally before each `await` in both `loadFirstPage()` and `_fetchMore()`, and discard the result (return without emitting) if the captured generation no longer matches `_generation` by the time the call resolves.

3. **Unguarded `DateTime.parse(entry.occurredAt)` can crash the screen on malformed data** — `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry_date_group.dart`'s `groupEntriesByDate()`, and `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart`'s `_formatTime()`. Wrap each parse in try/catch, mirroring the defensive pattern `EntriesRepositoryImpl._offlineFallback()` already uses around its own `DateTime.parse` calls. On a parse failure: `groupEntriesByDate()` should skip that entry rather than throwing (one corrupt cached entry shouldn't take down the whole list); `_formatTime()` should return a safe placeholder (e.g. `'--:--'`) instead of throwing.

4. **Unbatched Hive writes in `list()`** — `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart`. Replace the `for` loop calling `_entriesBox.put()` once per item with a single `_entriesBox.putAll({for (final dto in page.items) dto.id: dto.toJson()})` call, so a page's cache write is one batch instead of N sequential writes that can partially apply on a mid-loop failure.

5. **Missing test coverage: origin marking is only ever exercised for `EntrySource.manual`** — every `Entry` built anywhere in `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`/`meus_registros_cubit_test.dart` uses `EntrySource.manual`. Add coverage (in `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`, or a new `test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card_test.dart`) asserting each of the four `EntrySource` values (manual/audio/photo/chat) renders `EntryRecordCard` with its correct mapped icon and spine color.

6. **Missing test coverage: day-group labels ("Hoje"/"Ontem"/date) are never asserted** — `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s grouping test only checks card count, never the rendered label text. Add a test with one entry dated today, one dated yesterday, and one older, asserting `find.text('Hoje')`, `find.text('Ontem')`, and the `dd/mm/yyyy` fallback each render.

7. **Dead `clearNextCursor` parameter** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_state.dart`. `MeusRegistrosLoaded.copyWith`'s `clearNextCursor` parameter is never passed `true` anywhere in the codebase. Remove it and the branch that uses it.

8. **Defensive guard against a degenerate server response** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart`'s `_fetchMore()`. If a successful `loadMore()` page yields zero genuinely-new entries (every returned item was already present by id) while the server still reports a non-null `nextCursor`, treat it as exhausted (`nextCursor: null`) rather than trusting the server's cursor — otherwise a misbehaving/stuck server cursor could make the scroll listener keep re-triggering `loadMore()` indefinitely with no progress.

9. **Misleading test comment claims coverage that doesn't exist** — `test/core/widgets/back_arrow_header_test.dart`'s doc comment claims "spec-4-1 later gave `MeusRegistrosScreen` its own dedicated coverage of the same thing" (back arrow navigates home) — no such test exists in `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`. Add that test to `meus_registros_screen_test.dart` (mirroring the deleted `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen` test this diff removed from `placeholder_screens_test.dart`): tap the back arrow, assert navigation to `/`.

When done, report what you changed, the verification output, and anything left incomplete or risky.

---
title: 'Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'in-review'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: '8e5c168858c9ad6eb85b6b1772c7f933245ae6c3'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Entries from text/audio/photo capture (Epic 3) are invisible — "Meus Registros" is still the Epic 1 placeholder, and `EntriesRepository` only has `create`.

**Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by day, each card marked by origin. Extend `EntriesRepository` with paginated `list()`, falling back to Hive when offline. No sync badge, no tap-to-detail, no search/filter — those are 4.2/4.4/Epic 5.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.list({cursor, limit = 20})` → `Either<Failure, EntriesPage>`. Server assumed newest-first by `occurredAt` (undocumented, decided per AGENTS.md policy).
- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` → fall back to a full `entries` Hive box dump, sorted `occurredAt` desc, `nextCursor: null`. Other failures propagate as `Left`.
- Successful page persists to the Hive box, same "persist then return" shape `create()` uses.
- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.
- Card spine by `EntrySource`, exact hex match to prototype's `sourceMeta`: manual→`colorPrimary`, audio→`colorSecondary`, photo→`colorTextSecondary`, chat→`colorAccent`. Plus source icon, time, excerpt. No badge, not tappable.
- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.

**Ask First:** None — open calls are pinned above.

**Never:** sync badge (4.2), tap/detail nav (4.4), filters/search (Epic 5, tags), pull-to-refresh, any repository method beyond `list`/`create`, polished empty-state CTA (4.3 — plain "no entries" text only).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| First load, online | Screen opens | Skeleton past 300ms, then grouped list | N/A |
| Scroll pagination | Near list end, `nextCursor != null` | Next page appended, no dup ids | Fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry |
| Offline fallback | `list()` returns offline/timeout | Cached entries shown, sorted desc | N/A |
| Other failure | e.g. `authExpired` | Error state rendered | Global overlay or inline retry |
| Zero entries | Empty page + empty cache | Plain "no entries yet" text | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list()` to the one-method port
- `entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` -- `occurredAt` stays raw ISO string, parsed only for grouping
- `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` -- `create()`'s mirror shape for `list()`
- `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- `create()`'s call/error-map shape to mirror
- `entries/entries_injection.dart` -- add `MeusRegistrosCubit` registration
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` -- `get(function, {queryParameters})` already fits
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` -- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` = fallback triggers
- `lib/core/resource.dart` -- doc excludes RF07 from `Resource<T>`
- `app_router.dart:118-120`, `placeholder_screens.dart:159-182` -- route + placeholder
- `placeholder_screens.dart:355-397` (`_KanbanCard`) -- spine-card structure to mirror
- `placeholder_screens.dart:18-58` (`BootSplashScreen`) -- 300ms skeleton-delay pattern
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` -- reused as-is
- `openapi.yaml:480-645` -- `entries-list`: `cursor`/`limit`, `{data, meta.nextCursor}`

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `entries/domain/entities/entries_page.dart` -- new `EntriesPage{items, nextCursor}`
- [x] `entries/domain/entities/entry_date_group.dart` -- new `EntryDateGroup{date, entries}` + pure `groupEntriesByDate()`
- [x] `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list({cursor, limit = 20})`
- [x] `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `list()` via `ApiClient.get('entries-list', ...)`
- [x] `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` -- implement `list()` incl. offline fallback
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/skeleton_box.dart` -- new generic shimmer, tokens-only
- [x] `entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_{state,cubit}.dart` -- new, `loadFirstPage()`/`loadMore()`
- [x] `entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart` -- new, mirrors `_KanbanCard`, no tap handler
- [x] `entries/presentation/widgets/entry_skeleton_card.dart` -- new, from `SkeletonBox`
- [x] `entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart` -- new, scroll pagination + skeleton delay + grouped list
- [x] `entries/entries_injection.dart` -- register `MeusRegistrosCubit` as `lazySingleton`
- [x] `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart` -- route builds `MeusRegistrosScreen(cubit: sl())`
- [x] `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` -- delete `MeusRegistrosPlaceholderScreen`
- [x] Tests: grouping edge cases (midnight boundary, empty), `list()` datasource/repository incl. offline, cubit, screen (skeleton timing, pagination, zero/error)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a successful load with multi-day entries, when rendered, then the list is grouped by day with each card's spine colored by `EntrySource`.
- Given offline, when the screen loads, then cached entries render with no crash or duplicates.
- Given a session expiry while visible, when the global overlay appears, then scroll position is preserved and nothing throws.

## Design Notes

Code-review clarification (not a frozen-intent change): the Boundaries' offline/timeout Hive-fallback rule and the I/O matrix's "Scroll pagination: fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry" row only fully co-exist when the fallback is scoped to `cursor == null` (the first/fresh page). `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` must apply `_offlineFallback()` only for that case; a paginated call (`cursor != null`) that fails with `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` propagates as `Left` like any other pagination failure, so `MeusRegistrosCubit._fetchMore()`'s existing `loadMoreFailed`/retry path handles it uniformly — otherwise a connectivity drop mid-scroll silently merges an unrelated full-cache dump into the paginated list and breaks its newest-first ordering.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- Airplane mode with entries cached, reopen screen, confirm cached list renders instead of an error.
